question: What is the main goal of carrying out a community diagnosis in midwifery?

options.A: To provide free drugs to every household in the district
options.B: To replace the national census figures with local estimates
options.C: To identify local health problems and available community resources
options.D: To punish health workers who fail to meet hospital targets

explanation: A community diagnosis helps find out what health challenges exist locally and what resources are already available to support care. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why does a midwife in Nigeria need to look beyond the clinic walls to understand maternal health?

options.A: Community members refuse to visit clinics unless forced by traditional rulers
options.B: Home environments and cultural practices heavily influence health-seeking habits
options.C: Midwives are legally required to live in the village where they work
options.D: Hospital records are always completely accurate without needing outside checks

explanation: Things outside the clinic, like transport and local traditions, strongly affect how and when women decide to seek maternity care. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of secondary data used in a community diagnosis?

options.A: Existing antenatal clinic attendance registers from the local health post
options.B: Notes taken during a focus group discussion with young mothers
options.C: Direct observations made while walking through the village market
options.D: Brand new answers from a household survey you conduct today

explanation: Secondary data is information that was already collected by someone else before you started, such as clinic logbooks and past health reports. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h2)

question: A midwife wants to know why elderly women in the community discourage hospital deliveries. Which method works best?

options.A: Reviewing the monthly drug stock inventory at the pharmacy
options.B: Counting the number of antenatal beds available in the ward
options.C: Conducting focus group discussions with the elderly women
options.D: Measuring the weight of newborns delivered in the clinic

explanation: Focus group discussions provide a safe space to talk directly with groups and understand their underlying beliefs and attitudes. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the correct action when a midwife is analyzing raw community health data?

options.A: Organize and compare the numbers against targets or past records to find gaps
options.B: Change the figures to match the expectations of local politicians
options.C: Destroy all records that show poor health outcomes in the district
options.D: Hide the results so that community members do not panic

explanation: Analyzing data means organizing the raw numbers and comparing them to past records or goals to spot actual health issues. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is it important for a midwife to compare current health data with past records?

options.A: It ensures that no new babies are born with low birth weight
options.B: It proves that health problems never change across different generations
options.C: It is the only way to convince the government to pay staff salaries
options.D: It helps determine if health interventions are improving outcomes over time

explanation: Looking at data over time shows if health programs are actually making a positive difference or if the situation is getting worse. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which factor is normally considered first when prioritizing community health needs?

options.A: The severity and urgency of the health problem
options.B: The personal favorite color of the local government chairman
options.C: The brand of medical equipment available in private hospitals
options.D: The amount of time the midwife wants to spend on vacation

explanation: Health workers look at how severe and urgent an issue is to decide which life-threatening problems need attention first. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why should community members be involved when deciding which health needs to tackle first?

options.A: To ensure the chosen priority matches what the people feel is most important
options.B: To make sure the midwife does not have to do any paperwork
options.C: To prevent community members from ever complaining about the clinic
options.D: To shift all financial responsibility away from the health ministry

explanation: Involving the community ensures that everyone agrees on the plan and that real local needs are addressed rather than guessed ones. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h4)

question: Who are some of the key stakeholders to involve during community health mobilization in Nigeria?

options.C: Foreign embassy staff living in the capital city
options.D: International tourists visiting the local market

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are respected figures who can help encourage the community to support new health programs. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h5)

question: A midwife notices pregnant women are skipping clinic referrals due to cultural beliefs. What is a good first step?

options.A: Ignore the cultural beliefs and focus entirely on drug distribution
options.B: Report all pregnant women to the local police station for disobedience
options.C: Consult with respected community and religious leaders to discuss the issue
options.D: Close down the primary healthcare clinic until attitudes change

explanation: Working with community leaders helps bridge cultural divides and encourages families to trust safe maternal healthcare. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is an essential part of an actionable community health plan?

options.A: An exclusive focus on buying expensive imported equipment
options.B: Strict rules that punish patients who arrive late
options.C: A promise that no health problems will ever happen again
options.D: Clear objectives, assigned responsibilities, and timelines

explanation: A good plan needs clear goals, specific duties assigned to team members, and a timeline to keep activities moving forward. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why must monitoring and evaluation be part of any community health plan?

options.A: To track progress and see if the interventions are working as intended
options.B: To prove that the midwife did all the work without help
options.C: To give the health ministry a reason to cut clinic funding
options.D: To ensure that no community members ask questions about the budget

explanation: Monitoring helps health workers check whether their plan is meeting its targets and make changes when something is not working. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h6)
